A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, table, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching the relocated die-roll experiments.

before.justification: v1 reports original coin-flip and die-roll experiments, model-scaling results, fitted Bayesian discount factors, and attention analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds cutoff-dependent analyses and a corrected longer-rollout figure.

M1.justification: Token-probability extraction, linear normalization, Bayesian filtering, discounted updates, and L-BFGS-B fitting remain unchanged. The attention-experiment revision concerns evaluation conditions rather than a new model or inference method.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 changes the reported temporal input scenario from a central theta1 block surrounded by theta2 samples to a theta1 prefix followed by theta2 samples. Coin-flip and six-sided-die task coverage otherwise remains unchanged; the dice experiments move from Appendix F to G.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same language models, instruction-tuned variants, Pythia scales, and classical versus discounted Bayesian filters. Newly cited calibration and vision-language research is not added as evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 replaces the central-block sampling description with a sequential switchover protocol, retaining N=100 and explicitly specifying K=50 and variation from 10 to 90. This establishes a reported protocol revision, but does not establish that the unchanged main attention plots were rerun.

E4.justification: New Appendix F examines whether cutoff position affects attention-calibration relationships and prediction deviations through Figures F.1-F.3. Figure E.1 also supplies corrected graphical evidence for the longer-convergence analysis already described in v1.

E5.justification: Existing prompt-based standard-deviation reporting and attention correlation coefficients and p-values remain unchanged. The added cutoff plots and nonsignificance statement do not specify a new uncertainty-estimation or testing procedure; Figure F.3's shaded bands are not defined.

E6.justification: Figure E.1 replaces v1's duplicated 100-step trajectories with actual 200-step trajectories, although both captions already described 200 samples. Appendix F adds cutoff-specific findings, including larger deviations at extreme probabilities and reportedly nonsignificant differences across K. Main plots and Table 1 values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The Beta-binomial derivation, discounted-update equations, probability normalization, and mathematical arguments in Appendix C are retained. The revised sampling description concerns experimental settings; no new theorem, proof, or theoretical derivation appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and central conclusion retain the same claims about biased priors, the importance of in-context evidence, approximately Bayesian updating, and weak association between attention magnitude and update quality.

C2.justification: v2 connects discounting to previously reported long-context losses, adds arguments linking calibration to simulation quality and fairness, and suggests hidden miscalibration as an explanation for vision-language failures. The substantive limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a project-page link advertising code and visualizations, whereas v1 only promises a future MIT-licensed code release. Appendix A retains that future-release wording. Model specifications, normalization instructions, chat templates, and prompt lists remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Tian et al. (2023), Petryk et al. (2024), and Rahmanzadehgervi et al. (2025), and expands its relationship to the already-cited Liu et al. (2024). These extend calibration and multimodal positioning without changing the central Bayesian-ICL framing.

P1.justification: Edits are localized to related work, the attention setup, discussion, and acknowledgments. Appendix E's explanatory paragraph is reorganized, a new Appendix F is inserted, and the dice appendix becomes G; the main narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds three cutoff-analysis figures, replaces Figure E.1 with a 200-step display, and clarifies the captions of Figures 8-9. Existing figures and Table 1 are reflowed or relocated, while their main visual content is retained.

improvement.justification: Correcting Figure E.1 resolves a concrete mismatch between the claimed longer rollout and its evidence. Appendix F adds useful sensitivity evidence, and the project-page link improves access information. These are limited gains: the core results remain unchanged, the revised attention setup is not reconciled with the retained plots, and the cutoff nonsignificance claim lacks a specified test.
